vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: sparki-video-editor
Version: 1.0.6

The sparki-video-editor skill is a legitimate CLI wrapper for the Sparki AI video editing service (sparki.io). It facilitates video processing workflows including file uploads, style-guided editing, and result downloads via a structured REST API (agent-api.sparki.io). The implementation uses standard Python libraries (httpx, typer, pydantic) and follows secure coding practices, with no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection instructions.

llm.summary: The skill's code and runtime instructions mostly match an AI video-editing CLI, but there are a few inconsistencies (a mysterious required binary and no install spec despite bundled Python code) that warrant caution before installing.

dimensions.detail: The name/description, declared primaryEnv (SPARKI_API_KEY), network endpoints (agent-api.sparki.io) and CLI commands all line up with an AI video-editing service. However, the manifest declares a required binary 'uv' and an install step 'uv sync' even though the included code is a Python CLI (pyproject.toml and src/...). This binary requirement is not referenced within the Python code and is disproportionate/unexplained.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent to use the included sparki CLI to upload/edit/download videos and to proactively surface the skill on video-related requests. It does not instruct reading unrelated files or exfiltrating system secrets beyond the Sparki API key and local files explicitly supplied by the user. It also explicitly forbids accepting direct video attachments in chat and prescribes upload flows.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Registry metadata lists 'No install spec' but the package contains a pyproject and full Python source. There is an embedded 'install' entry mapping 'uv' to 'uv sync' in SKILL.md metadata; this points to an external tool named 'uv' (not a standard system tool) and the manifest lacks instructions for installing the Python dependencies (typer, httpx, pydantic). This inconsistency could lead to unclear runtime behavior (how/where the code is executed) and is an installation risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill only requires a single primary credential (SPARKI_API_KEY). The code also optionally reads SPARKI_UPLOAD_TG_LINK and stores config/history under ~/.openclaw. No other unrelated credentials or broad environment access are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill only persists its own config/history under ~/.openclaw; it does not request system-wide privileges or modify other skills. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement a legitimate Sparki CLI that talks to sparki servers and only requires your Sparki API key. Two things to verify before installing: (1) The manifest requires a binary named 'uv' and lists an install step 'uv sync' but the included code is Python — ask the provider what 'uv' is, why it's needed, and how the Python dependencies will be installed and run in your agent environment. (2) Confirm you trust the SPARKI_API_KEY destination (DEFAULT_BASE_URL is agent-api.sparki.io and the homepage is sparki.io). If you proceed, avoid pasting sensitive keys into chat: prefer providing the key via environment variable or a vault, and review the ~/.openclaw/sparki.json file after setup. If the publisher cannot explain the 'uv' requirement or provide clear install/run instructions, treat the package as untrusted.
